text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

Abstract (172 words):  
In this study, we aimed to clarify whether the GEO accession GSE309890 is the same entity as GDS309890. We queried the NCBI GEO database to resolve these two accessions and retrieved metadata regarding each record’s unique identifier (UID), entry type (Series or Dataset), and associated FTP directory. Queries were executed using the geo_resolve_accession function to ensure accurate matching of each accession. The results indicate that GSE309890 is distinct from GDS309890, as they have different UIDs (200309890 for GSE309890 and 309890 for GDS309890) and different record types. GSE309890 is a GEO Series, while GDS309890 is a curated GEO Dataset. These two records each have their own FTP directories and metadata. This distinction between Series and Dataset designations is important for researchers selecting appropriate data types for reanalysis or integration into broader studies. Establishing the differences between these accessions—and using consistent, accurate referencing of GEO records—helps ensure data integrity and clarity. Future data analyses will benefit from accurately identifying the unique roles and content of GSE and GDS records.

I. Introduction  
Background. The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) is an NCBI-hosted resource containing gene expression datasets (Series, Samples, Platforms, and curated DataSets). Each type of record has its own accession prefix, for instance “GSE” for Series and “GDS” for curated GEO DataSets. Researchers sometimes encounter different prefixes like GSE and GDS with similar numbers and wonder whether the entries represent the same dataset.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. It was unclear if GSE309890 and GDS309890 pointed to the same record or two different entries.  
Objective & Hypothesis. The objective was to compare the metadata of GSE309890 and GDS309890 to determine if they represent the same record. We hypothesized that the distinct prefixes would indicate two different records despite the similar numeric portion of their accessions.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. Our approach was to check the official NCBI GEO service to compare unique identifiers and record types for each accession.  
Materials. We used the geo_resolve_accession function to query the NCBI GEO database for GSE309890 and GDS309890.  
Procedures.  
1) We called geo_resolve_accession with arguments: {accessions: "GSE309890,GDS309890"}.  
2) We examined the results, focusing on the “uid,” “accession,” and “entry_type” fields.  
Statistical Analysis. We did not perform numerical computations or statistical analyses in resolving these GEO records.

III. Results  
Data Presentation.  
Table 1. Resolution results from the geo_resolve_accession call:

| Query       | UID        | Accession  | Entry_Type | FTP_Directory_URL                        |
|-------------|------------|------------|------------|-------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890   | 200309890  | GSE309890  | GSE        | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/ |
| GDS309890   | 309890     | GDS309890  | GDS        | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/ |

Findings. The function returned distinct record types and unique identifiers: GSE309890 has UID 200309890 and is a GEO Series, whereas GDS309890 has UID 309890 and is a curated GEO DataSet. They possess different FTP directories and are therefore separate records.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. The retrieved metadata indicates that GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not the same record in GEO. The “GSE” prefix references a Series, while the “GDS” prefix references a curated DataSet, each with a unique assigned UID.  
Context. The discrepancy arises from GEO’s record types: GSE (Series) and GDS (DataSet) reflect different organizational structures in how GEO data is stored and curated.  
Limitations. We have only reviewed the official GEO metadata as obtained through the geo_resolve_accession function, and no additional references were identified in PubMed for further context.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 and GDS309890 are separate records. Accurate identification of GEO record types is critical for proper data usage. Future work might involve exploring the relationship between the respective Series and DataSet or verifying further sample-level details (e.g., GSM accessions).

References  
No references were retrieved for this query.

Acknowledgments  
We acknowledge the NCBI GEO database and the geo_resolve_accession function for providing the metadata used in this study.
